_README: Copy this to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (create the directory if the agy
CLI has never run). PER MACHINE - it is not in this repo's checkout path and does not
travel with a clone.
WHY IT MATTERS. With no settings file the agy CLI starts with permissions=<nil> and
toolPermission=request-review, and headless mode auto-denies every shell command
because it cannot prompt anyone. The turn still returns status SUCCESS with an empty
response and exit code 0, so the seat looks like it had nothing to say. Verified
2026-09-15: creating this file flips the CLI's startup log from permissions=<nil> to
permissions=&{Allow:[...]}, which settles GitHub issue #548 - allow-rules ARE honoured
headless in agy 1.2.3, and that issue is stale.
RULE SYNTAX. command(x) matches by prefix, so command(git) covers git add, git log and
so on. Do NOT write unsandboxed(...) rules even though a stderr message may tell you
to: the binary states 'unsandboxed is no longer a valid rule, use command() instead'.
File reads inside a detected workspace (a git repo) are auto-allowed and need no rule;
a directory that is not a workspace is outside that grant and will be denied.
THIS FILE IS NOT THE WHOLE FIX. Two other things were needed to make a tool-using
headless turn complete in 40 seconds instead of timing out at 5m30s having burned
195,056 input tokens for an empty reply:
1. --new-project on the invocation. Without it the CLI resumes the project's
persisted model from conversation_summaries.db and ignores --model, which is how
a reasoning tier got selected and thought for five minutes.
2. A prompt giving exact file paths and forbidding directory search. When the find
tool hits a context deadline the agent falls back to recursive list_dir and burns
context without bound - that, not permissions, was the token burn.
Both are already in the GEMPRO seat in seats.example.jsonc.
Delete the _README key before use if you prefer; the CLI ignores unknown keys, but it
is noise in a config you will read again.
